---
title: "00 — small RNA preprocessing and miRDeep2 discovery"
output:
  github_document: default
---

This is the command-line part of the workflow that happened before the R analysis files. It prepares the genome reference, collapses and maps the small-RNA reads, and runs miRDeep2 to generate the raw candidate table used in Step 01.

For software details, see the [miRDeep2 documentation](https://www.mdc-berlin.de/content/mirdeep2-documentation), the [miRDeep2 GitHub repository](https://github.com/rajewsky-lab/mirdeep2), and the [Bowtie manual](https://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/manual.shtml).

## Main inputs

- `GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.fna`
- `config_2025.txt`
- `known_cnidarian_mature_miRNAs.fasta`

## 1. Clean genome FASTA headers if needed

The genome FASTA used for mapping needed headers without spaces.

```bash
GENOME="GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.fna"

# Strip trailing description text from FASTA headers so the genome identifiers
# stay simple during the mapping and discovery steps.
if grep -qE '^>.*[[:space:]]' "${GENOME}"; then
  sed '/^>/ s/[[:space:]].*$//' "${GENOME}" >             GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.noSpace.fna
fi
```

## 2. Build the Bowtie index

The first argument is the genome FASTA and the second is the basename used for the Bowtie index files written from that reference.

```bash
bowtie-build \
  GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.fna \
  GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.fna
```

## 3. Collapse, trim, and map reads with `mapper.pl`

This step uses the sample manifest and genome index to generate the collapsed read FASTA and the `.arf` mapping file required by miRDeep2.

In this command, `-k TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG` is the 3' adapter sequence that was trimmed from the small-RNA reads, `-l 18` keeps reads that were at least 18 nt after trimming, `-p` points to the Bowtie genome index, `-s` writes the collapsed read FASTA, and `-t` writes the genome-mapping `.arf` file. The remaining single-letter flags follow the standard `mapper.pl` usage described in the miRDeep2 documentation linked above.

```bash
# Collapse identical reads, trim the adapter, and map the retained reads to the
# genome before the miRDeep2 discovery step.
mapper.pl \
  config_2025.txt \
  -d -e -i -j \
  -k TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG \
  -l 18 \
  -h -m -n \
  -p GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.fna \
  -s reads6.fa \
  -t reads_vs_genome6.arf
```

## 4. Run miRDeep2 discovery

The main project-specific inputs in this command are the collapsed reads, the genome FASTA used for mapping, the `.arf` mapping file, and the curated known-miRNA FASTA. For the detailed meaning of the remaining miRDeep2 arguments, see the miRDeep2 documentation linked above.

```bash
# Use the collapsed reads, genome mappings, and curated known-miRNA reference
# to score candidate precursors in the miRDeep2 run.
miRDeep2.pl \
  reads6.fa \
  GCA_000222465.2_Adig_1.1_genomic.noSpace.fna \
  reads_vs_genome6.arf \
  known_cnidarian_mature_miRNAs.fasta \
  none \
  none \
  -g -1
```

## Output carried into Step 01

The key output of this step was the raw miRDeep2 result table:

- `result_23_11_2025_t_13_41_12.xlsx`

The later `quantifier.pl` command is shown in Step 01 because it used the mature-miRNA FASTA created only after the naming step was finished.
